Usage: oe <command> [arguments] [global flags]

Commands:
  new            Create a project and its Sandbox environment, then write open-e2ee.config.ts, the Relay connection in .env.local, and the @open-e2ee/oe devDependency.
  auth           Log in with a browser and store the session in the OS keychain, then accept the OpenE2EE terms for the organization. --organization ORG puts the session in that organization. Without it, a person at a terminal who belongs to more than one organization chooses one. In an app directory with no config, a person at a terminal then creates a project, links one, or skips. Show the session and its organizations, or remove the session.
      Also: oe auth
  org            Show the organization of the current session, list the organizations of the account, or move the stored session to another organization. ORG is an ID or a unique name. Without ORG, a person at a terminal chooses one. A session from OE_ACCESS_TOKEN or an agent session cannot switch.
      Also: oe org, oe org view, oe orgs, oe organizations
  doctor         Check the config, session, project, and Relay connection of the selected environment. With --wait, then wait for the first acknowledged Sandbox message.
  identity       Check a public draft identity profile. External ES256 checks send a fresh registration assertion from stdin to the authenticated Console verifier. The assertion is transient. Device-owned checks use no assertion. Results are historical and do not verify installed configuration, device admission, member binding, exchange or lifecycle.
  link           Link this directory to a Relay project that exists and write the Relay connection of each active environment to its env file. With no config, write open-e2ee.config.ts from the server policy. Without PROJECT, rewrite only the env files.
  project        Show the linked Relay project, list the projects of the organization of the session, show usage, or print a Relay connection URL.
      Also: oe projects, oe apps, oe app list, oe projects list, oe apps list, oe project, oe app, oe project view [PROJECT], oe app show [PROJECT], oe app view [PROJECT], oe app usage [PROJECT], oe app connection [PROJECT]
  config         Keep open-e2ee.config.ts and the console in step. push applies the environment sections: Sandbox, then Production when the file has its section. pull writes the Relay policy of each active environment into the file with the fewest changes. A Production change or a replaced value needs --yes or a person's answer. --dry-run changes nothing.
  notifications  Stage and verify best-effort iOS notification profiles.
      Also: oe notifications
  agent          Install the OpenE2EE skills for coding agents: write .agents/skills/<name> and link .claude/skills/<name> to it, or write a copy when a link fails. The project scope uses the directory of open-e2ee.config.ts, else the working directory, and --scope user uses the home directory. --check reports each skill as current, missing, or changed, and writes nothing.
      Also: oe agent, oe agent status
  version        Print the CLI version.
  help           Show all commands, or the usage of one command.

Global flags (before or after the command):
  --json
      Write one JSON document to stdout for the result, for success and for failure. oe auth login writes one pending event before it, while a person approves the device.
  --json-stream
      Write newline-delimited JSON progress events, then one final event, to stdout.
  --agent yes|no|auto
      Say whether a coding agent runs oe. The default, auto, reads the environment variables that coding agents set. Under an agent, the default output is JSON, and oe never prompts and never opens a browser. --agent no restores text output.
  --env sandbox|production
      Select the environment. -e is the short form. Without it, doctor, identity, project, and notifications read OE_ENV, then use sandbox. config pull reads each active environment, and config push applies each section of the config; --env narrows either to one.
  --control-url URL
      Use another control API. It must use HTTPS except on loopback.
  -h, --help
      Show help.
  --version
      Print the CLI version.

  1  The command failed. The error and its code tell why.
  2  The command line is invalid or a required input is missing.
  4  Authentication is required. Run next, which is oe auth login, with --organization ORG after a failed switch. ACCESS_TOKEN_INVALID has no next: set OE_ACCESS_TOKEN to a new token, or unset it and run oe auth login.
  5  A person must act before the command can continue. The error tells what to do. When action.url is present, it is the page that the person opens.
  6  The failure is temporary. It is safe to run the same command again later. next is that command.

      The scopes of OE_ACCESS_TOKEN, separated by commas or spaces.
  OE_PROTECTION_BYPASS
      A protection bypass secret for the control URL. Login stores it with that session. It takes precedence over the stored bypass and never appears in output.
  OE_ENV
      The environment of doctor, identity, project, and notifications when --env is not given: sandbox or production. new and config ignore it.

name: help config
stdout:

A Production change or a replaced value needs --yes or a person's answer. --dry-run changes nothing.

  oe config push [--env sandbox|production] [--yes] [--dry-run]
  oe config pull [--env sandbox|production] [--yes] [--dry-run]
